question: When can a downstream reader untangle a local crossing after a summary of the two strands?
inputs: Every reversible gate on a pair of bits; one named signed swap and one ternary quandle crossing; all joint relations, all point states, and a public menu followed by a future stop/undo choice.
forbidden_inputs: No actual future query in the encoder, no uncharged intermediate state in a projected-only message, no fitted parameters.
mapping: Exhaustive permutation, relation and answer-signature evaluation. Test both sides of the braid relation on adjacent positions and undo with each candidate's inverse.
primary_observable: Reversible recovery, dependence on both inputs, collision of separate marginals, minimum payload for known or delayed reader, and bounded optimal one-bit delayed accuracy.
comparators_or_controls: Exact joint relation vs separate allowed-value sets, same crossing repeated vs inverse, known vs delayed read, and all two-bit bijections.
resource_budget: A single deterministic CPU census, at most 512 joint relations per candidate and 24 candidate binary gates.
first_executable_signal: Two joint relations can have exactly the same two marginals after crossing while the reader needs opposite answers after undo.
stop_rule: Report all candidates and both wiring and readout regimes even when the alternatives agree.
